mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during an expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for two consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer sentiment (proxied by RSAFS) above 5 points month-over-month indicates restrictive monetary policy coinciding with reduced consumer confidence, which amplifies downside risk and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND RSAFS falls > 5 points MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals strengthening residential demand, which boosts construction-related equities and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average and a fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and inflation risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND UNRATE < 3.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) below its 3-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a broad-based manufacturing slowdown, which reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.
